operative_quotes:
1. Each player takes an action card and all pieces of one player color. Put every scoring chip on **0**. Choose a banker; put money and tiles within reach.
2. Remove **End of Game** from the property deck and shuffle the remaining cards. Deal **2 cards per player**. With two players, discard and replace any F-lot setup card, so each player receives two valid A–E initial properties.
3. Put one of your markers on each of your two initial lots. Take money from the bank equal to the **sum of the printed money values on your two cards**. These card money values apply **only during setup**. Discard the cards into their corresponding color/Strip spaces with counts easily visible.
4. Divide the remaining shuffled deck into **4 roughly equal stacks**. Put End of Game **on top of the fourth stack**, then put the other three stacks above it. Place the resulting draw pile beside the board.
5. Each player rolls **2 dice**. The highest roller takes the player card and the first turn. After each turn, pass it to the player on the **left**.
answers.answer: Each player starts with two lots and money equal to the sum of the two cards’ printed money values; those values apply only during setup. Discard dealt cards to their color/Strip spaces. Remove End of Game, split the rest into four roughly equal stacks, place End of Game atop stack four, then put the other three stacks above it.

Each normal turn has **Draw**, then **Play**: draw a property card, acquire its lot or die, pay every marked lot, pay money and score points for the indicated casinos, discard the card in its appropriate pile, then take actions in Play. Trading is also possible at any time, subject to the restrictions below.

1. **Draw a property card and take over its space before payouts.** If it is an empty lot, put your marker there. If it contains another player’s sprawled tile and die, replace their die with your own **at the same current pip value**, not the board’s printed value. If the tile has no die, add your die at the **printed board value**. If your own die already occupies it, leave it unchanged. The casino tile stays in place. Apply the dice/marker supply rules if necessary and settle any boss tie before paying casinos.
2. **All owned lots pay:** every lot with a marker pays its owner **$1 from the bank**, including the newly acquired lot, regardless of the card’s color or whose turn it is. Casino tiles do not also collect lot income.
3. **The indicated casinos pay money and points:** a single-color card pays every casino of that color anywhere on the board. A **Pay The Strip** card instead pays every casino with at least **one edge adjacent to The Strip**, regardless of color. A qualifying casino pays for **all its tiles**, not only the tile touching The Strip.
4. **Money:** each player receives **$1 per pip on each of their dice** in a paying casino, including players who are not its boss. **Points:** only the casino’s boss receives **1 point per tile** in that casino. Follow the scoring-break and separate-casino rules below.
5. Discard the property card in its appropriate color/Strip pile so the number already drawn remains countable. Proceed to Play, except that two-player F cards repeat Draw as described below.

On your own turn you may **build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize and gamble** in **any order**, or stop taking actions. You may repeat actions except **gamble is limited to once per turn**, and **no die may be reorganized more than once per turn**. You must be able to pay the stated action cost. After each action check for boss ties and settle them before continuing.
answers.answer: Highest roller starts; pass the player card left after each turn. A normal turn draws and resolves a property card before Play actions; take actions in any order and stop when done.

operative_quotes: A **lot** is a board space without a casino tile. Your marker on a lot makes it yours. Once built, it is a casino space, no longer a lot; your die on its tile represents your ownership/influence there.

A **casino** is one tile or an edge-connected group of same-color tiles on the same block. Same-color edge neighbors merge immediately into one casino, even if their dice belong to different players. Diagonal contact alone does not connect them; casinos cannot be subdivided after joining.

The **boss** is the player owning the **highest individual die** in that casino, not the most dice or the highest sum of pips. Several highest dice belonging to the same player are sufficient to make that player boss. Resolve highest ties between different players immediately as described under **Boss ties**.
answers.answer: Same-color tiles sharing an edge on the same block merge immediately and cannot be subdivided; diagonal contact does not connect. Boss is the owner of the highest individual die, not the most dice or highest total pips.

answers.answer: Build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, and gamble may be taken in any order. Repeat except gamble once per turn and no die reorganized more than once. No action on another player’s turn.

operative_quotes: Choose **a lot you own**. Take back its marker, choose an **available** casino tile of any color, pay the **price printed on the lot**, and place the tile there. Put one of your dice on it with the **lot’s printed die value** face up. Edge-connected same-color tiles merge immediately; boss control may change.
answers.answer: Pay the printed $6 price, take back your marker, place an available tile of any color, and put your die at the lot’s printed value, 2.

operative_quotes: You must be **boss of the casino** you expand. Choose an **empty, unowned lot sharing an edge** with it, pay **twice that lot’s printed price**, and place an available tile of the **same color** there. Put your die on it at the **lot’s printed die value**. You cannot sprawl into another player’s marked lot, your own marked lot, a built space or a merely diagonal neighbor. Without an available tile of the required color, you cannot sprawl.
answers.answer: Pay twice $9 ($18), place an available gold tile and your die at 3. Only an empty, unowned edge-adjacent lot is legal; not an opponent-marked or diagonal lot.

operative_quotes: You must be **boss**. Choose a **new color with enough available tiles for the entire casino**. Pay **$5 per tile** and replace **every tile** of that casino with the new color, returning the old tiles to their supply. Dice stay with their holdings and keep their values. You cannot remodel just part of a casino.
answers.answer: A boss remodels the whole two-tile casino for $10 and needs two available tiles of the new color. Replace all tiles; dice and values stay. After merger, highest individual die determines boss; settle any cross-player highest tie immediately.

operative_quotes: You need **at least one die** in the casino; you **need not be boss** and may reorganize a casino containing only your dice.
answers.answer: A non-boss with one die may reorganize. Pay $10 for all pips (5+3+2), including opponents’ pips. All dice reroll; each player rolls their own. Return dice to their own original tiles; multiple own dice may be reassigned among those own tiles.

operative_quotes: You need **at least one die** in the casino; you **need not be boss** and may reorganize a casino containing only your dice.
answers.answer: A casino with any die already reorganized this turn cannot be reorganized again, even after merger. Free boss-tie rerolls do not use the paid reorganization allowance.

operative_quotes: If **two or more players** tie for the **highest** value in a casino, reroll **all dice currently tied for highest**, **for free**. Leave smaller dice untouched. Reassess the highest value across the whole casino after each roll. If different players still tie for the current highest, reroll the current highest dice again. Continue until only **one player** owns the highest value; several highest dice belonging to that one player need no reroll.
answers.answer: Reroll all current highest tied dice for free. If Red 5 and Blue 5 become 3 while Green 4 stays, Green is boss. Same-player highest dice need no reroll; ties among smaller dice do nothing.

operative_quotes: **Once during your own turn**, choose a casino where **another player is boss**, and give that player the **House card**. If no opponent bosses a casino, you cannot gamble. You may bet no more than **all three limits**: **$5 per tile in that casino**, **your available money**, and **the boss’s available money**.
answers.answer: Maximum bet is min($20, $18, $15) = $15. Give the House card to the boss. Gamble once at most on your turn.

operative_quotes:
| Dice sum | Result |
|---|---|
| 3, 4, 9, 10 or 11 | You win: the boss pays you **the bet amount**. You keep/get back your own stake. |
| 2 or 12 | You win double: the boss pays you **twice the bet**, limited to the money the boss actually has. You keep/get back your own stake. |
| 5, 6, 7 or 8 | You lose: pay **the bet amount** to the boss. |
answers.answer: Sums 3,4,9,10,11: boss pays $4. Sums 2 or 12: double is $8, but boss has $7, so pays $7. Sums 5,6,7,8: bettor pays $4. A winning bettor keeps/gets back their stake.

operative_quotes: Players may trade **at any time, even off-turn**, except during boss-tie resolution or after End of Game is drawn. Multiple players may participate. Trade any combination of **money, lots, dice in casinos and actions performed on the acting player’s current turn**.

For a transferred lot replace the owner’s marker with the recipient’s marker. For a transferred casino die replace it with the recipient’s die, retaining the **current pip value**, not the board’s printed die. A die trade can therefore change the boss and cause an immediate highest tie.

You **cannot trade points or casino tiles**, or promise actions, exchanges or transfers for **future turns**. **No player can perform an action on another player’s turn.** A current-turn action can be part of a trade only for the player whose turn it is. If something prevents an element of a trade from happening, the subsequent steps of that trade do not occur.
answers.answer: Trade any time except tie resolution or after End of Game; multiple players may participate. Lots transfer by marker replacement; dice by die replacement retaining current pips. Trade money, lots, casino dice, or current-turn actions of the acting player. Cannot trade points or tiles or promise future-turn actions, exchanges, or transfers; no actions on another player’s turn.

operative_quotes: Record casino points by moving your chip on the **printed scoring track**. Numeric gaps are **breaks**: you must earn enough **from that individual casino** to reach the next printed value. Stop before a break you cannot cross and lose unusable excess points; do not save them for later.

When several casinos pay you points on one turn, score them **individually, from smallest to largest**, choosing the order of equal-size casinos. You cannot combine their awards to cross a break. Several separate one-tile casinos therefore still cannot move a chip from 8 to 10.
answers.answer: From 8: 1→8, 2→10, 3→10, 4→12, 5→12. Separate one-tile casino awards cannot be combined. Score casinos individually smallest to largest; choose order among equal sizes.

operative_quotes: As soon as anyone draws **End of Game**, the game ends immediately. Do not take Play actions or initiate trades after that draw. Make the **final payout for all owned lots and all casinos touching The Strip**, using normal money, boss-point and scoring-break rules. Highest score after that payout wins. If tied for most points, the tied player with **most money** wins. The source gives no further tiebreak if both remain equal.
answers.answer: End of Game ends play immediately: no Play actions or initiated trades. Make final payout for owned lots and Strip-touching casinos, under normal rules. Highest score wins; tied score goes to most money, with no further stated tie-break. Immediate win also at 90+ points.

operative_quotes: **Do not build on F block.** During setup, **discard any F-lot card and draw a replacement**; use the two accepted A–E cards for starting lots and money. Discarded F cards remain discarded.
answers.answer: Setup: discard F and draw replacement; do not build on F. During a turn, F puts no marker but still resolves normal lot and casino payouts, then repeat Draw until A–E; no actions between draws. Multiple payouts before actions are possible.

2. Remove **End of Game** from the property deck and shuffle the remaining cards. Deal **2 cards per player**. With two players, discard and replace any F-lot setup card, so each player receives two valid A–E initial properties.
3. Put one of your markers on each of your two initial lots. Take money from the bank equal to the **sum of the printed money values on your two cards**. These card money values apply **only during setup**. Discard the cards into their corresponding color/Strip spaces with counts easily visible.
4. Divide the remaining shuffled deck into **4 roughly equal stacks**. Put End of Game **on top of the fourth stack**, then put the other three stacks above it. Place the resulting draw pile beside the board.
5. Each player rolls **2 dice**. The highest roller takes the player card and the first turn. After each turn, pass it to the player on the **left**.
